claim.text: 9,672 Omicron samples found in January, huge rise from December

fusion_ranked_evidence.title: 9,672 Omicron Samples Found in January in Genome Sequencing, Huge Rise from Dec: Govt | India News - News18
fusion_ranked_evidence.snippet: # 9,672 Omicron Samples Found in January in Genome Sequencing, Huge Rise from Dec: Govt. ## Addressing a press conference, NCDC Director Dr S K Singh said sub-lineages of Omicron - BA.1 and BA.2 were found in sequenced samples while BA.3 has not been found yet. As many as 9,672 Omicron samples were found in January in genome sequencing constituting 75 per cent of the total sequenced samples of COVID-19, a huge rise from the December figure of 1,292, the government said on Thursday. He further said that a huge rise from December has been seen in the number of Omicron samples in January. In January, 9,672 omicron samples were found which was about 75 per cent of total sequenced samples and AY lineage was found in 3,201 samples and Delta was found in 1,578 samples, he said. fusion_ranked_evidence.title: SARS-CoV-2 Omicron variant
fusion_ranked_evidence.snippet: | * Alpha (B.1.1.7) * Beta (B.1.351) * Gamma (P.1) * Delta (B.1.617.2)   Omicron (B.1.1.529)   * BA.1 (B.1.1.529.1) * BA.2 (B.1.1.529.2) * BA.3 (B.1.1.529.3) * BA.4 (B.1.1.529.4) * BA.5 (B.1.1.529.5) * XBB * BA.2.86 (B.1.1.529.2.86) * NB.1.8.1 * XFG * BA.3.2 (B.1.1.529.3.2) |. **Omicron** (B.1.1.529) is a heavily mutated variant of SARS-CoV-2 first reported to the World Health Organization (WHO) by the Network for Genomics Surveillance in South Africa on 24 November 2021. It was first detected in Botswana and has spread to become the predominant variant in circulation around the world. Following the original B.1.1.529 variant, several subvariants of Omicron have emerged, including: BA.1, BA.2, BA.3, BA.4, and BA.5. JN.1 went on to spawn multiple notable sublineages, including KP.3.1.1 and XEC in 2024, and LP.8.1, NB.1.8.1, and XFG in 2025. As of 25 June 2025, the variants of interest as specified by the World Health Organization are JN.1, and the variants under monitoring are KP.3, KP.3.1.1, JN.1.18, LP.8.1, NB.1.8.1, XEC and XFG.
